Alright, let me think through this year.

I've been doing wheat-maize on these 10.1 mu for decades. At my age, with just me and the old lady at home, we can't work like we used to — the kids are in the city and won't come back to help. So I keep things simple: same rotation as always, hire the combine at harvest, and don't try anything fancy.

**Wheat** (already in the ground since last October, harvest around June 10):
I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before sowing — that's my base. Used a semi-winter-hardy variety I've been growing for years, Jimai something, can't remember the number but the agro-store owner knows what I want. Planted after the maize came off, did a rotary tillage, sowed with a drill.

Right now it's spring, so I'm about to do the jointing topdressing — maybe 10-12 kg of urea per mu, depends how the field looks. If the color is good I'll lean lighter because urea got expensive again this year. I'll run the well once around topdressing time, once more at heading if there's no rain. Extension guy said we should do soil testing but I just go by how the wheat looks — 40 years of looking at wheat tells you more than a paper.

**Maize** (mid-June right after wheat combine, harvest late September):
No time to waste between wheat and maize — three, four days max. I no-till plant with a dedicated drill-fertilizer combo, puts seed and base fertilizer in at the same time. Use Zhengdan hybrid seed, buy fresh every year. About 35 kg compound at planting, then topdress 15 kg urea per mu at big-bell stage. One irrigation if July is dry, otherwise skip it — maize roots deep and summer rain usually comes.

Pests: I spray once on wheat for aphids in May, once on maize for borer around July. Herbicide at planting for both.

Labor — it's just us two. I hire the combine for wheat harvest and maize harvest, pay by the mu. The planting I do myself with the tractor.
